newsitem.title: USA: Operation to refloat tanker off Miami going slowly.
newsitem.headline: Operation to refloat tanker off Miami going slowly.

text.p: Salvage crews are working round the clock in a hazardous operation to refloat a tanker which ran aground in an aquatic preserve off Miami with a cargo of potentially explosive liquid gas, the U.S. Coast Guard said Friday.
"The nature of the grounding, the type of fuel and nature of the cargo is making the operation slow and tedious and it could last as long as two weeks," a Coast Guard statement said.

The German-flagged Igloo Moon hit the bottom on Wednesday about three miles south of Cape Florida, on Key Biscayne, in the Biscayne National Park. It was loaded with an estimated 6,500 tonnes of liquid butadiene, a highly-inflammable hydrocarbon used in making synthetic rubber.
So far there has been no pollution, the Coast Guard said.

Salvagers are trying to remove enough fuel and cargo from the Igloo Moon to refloat it. Overnight about 970 barrels of fuel -- more than 40,000 gallons -- were taken off the vessel. All fuel from tanks in contact with the ship's bottom is expected to be removed by sunset.
About 1,000 tonnes of the butadiene cargo need to be removed and the ship's owners are trying to find a suitable vessel to load it onto.
In anticipation of rough seas expected on Saturday, workers are ballasting the ship -- temporarily weighing it down by filling empty tanks with seawater.
The Igloo Moon was travelling from the Middle East to Houston went it became trapped on Wednesday. It is submerged in about 25 feet of water.
